import org.springframework.data.domain.Page;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;

import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.api.OwnerV2Api;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.OwnerPageDto;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service.ClinicService;
import org.springframework.security.access.prepost.PreAuthorize;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.CrossOrigin;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;

@RestController
@CrossOrigin(exposedHeaders = "errors, content-type")
@RequestMapping("/api")
public class OwnerRestControllerV2 implements OwnerV2Api {

    private final ClinicService clinicService;
    private final OwnerMapper ownerMapper;

    public OwnerRestControllerV2(ClinicService clinicService, OwnerMapper ownerMapper) {
        this.clinicService = clinicService;
        this.ownerMapper = ownerMapper;
    }

    @Override
    @PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
    public ResponseEntity<OwnerPageDto> listOwnersPage(String lastName, Integer page, Integer size) {
        int pageNumber = page == null ? 0 : page;
        int pageSize = size == null ? 20 : size;
        Page<Owner> owners = this.clinicService.findOwners(
            lastName,
            PageRequest.of(pageNumber, pageSize, Sort.by("id")));
        return new ResponseEntity<>(ownerMapper.toOwnerPageDto(owners), HttpStatus.OK);
    }
}

## Summary

I implemented the disposable-email-domain blocklist in `OwnerRestControllerV1.java` (the controller handling `POST /api/owners`):

1. **Added the blocklist constant** — `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` = `{mailinator.com, tempmail.com, guerrillamail.com}`, alongside the existing `EMAIL_PATTERN`.
2. **Added a `java.util.Set` import.**
3. **Wired the check into `normalizeAndValidateFields`** — right after the email is normalized (trimmed/lower-cased) and syntactically validated. If the domain is blocklisted, the method returns `false`, which the `addOwner` handler already translates into `400 BAD_REQUEST`.
4. **Added the `isDisposableEmailDomain` helper** that extracts the domain after the last `@` and tests membership case-insensitively (the email is already lower-cased by the caller).

I placed the check on the create flow's email validation path, matching where the specification's rule applies (the acceptance test posts `x@mailinator.com` and expects 400). Reusing the existing normalize-and-validate seam kept it consistent with how the other email/address/telephone rules reject with 400.

The targeted acceptance test (`errorRejectsDisposableDomain`) and the full test suite both pass.
